hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to distinct vertical linear features or elongated columns defined by high luminance contrast, typically appearing as a vertical strip of bright white light or a dark vertical structure against a contrasting background. The activating feature usually takes the form of a light gap between dark objects, a specular highlight on a cylindrical surface, an architectural pillar, or an elongated organic shape like a tassel or trunk. The dominant colors are monochromatic, consisting of bright white, silver, or light grey highlights contrasted against deep black, dark charcoal, or matte grey fields. The neuron remains invariant to semantic category (responding to both organic forms like feathers and fur, and synthetic objects like metal and plastic) and texture, provided the strict vertical orientation and sharp tonal boundary are preserved. The vertical feature typically spans 60–100% of the image height and is centered horizontally, occupying approximately 5–30% of the image width.
